facts.text: Half of revenue is now fee income negotiated with distributors and networks rather than advertising, which makes renewals the main business risk. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy is mixed: growth is funded partly with secured debt while shareholders are paid. The company bought stations for USD 280 million of stated consideration in the first half of 2026, issued USD 70 million of first lien notes to fund the American Spirit Media closing and a preferred stock repurchase, and paid common dividends of USD 33 million and preferred dividends of USD 52 million in FY2025. The preferred repurchase paid USD 30 million for USD 50 million of liquidation preference, which cut junior claims and the cash dividend by USD 4 million a year, but the new first lien debt ranks ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes. facts.text: The strongest evidence for a lower risk reading is the operating record and the preference for reducing junior claims: the preferred repurchase was done at a 40.00% discount to liquidation preference, the board authorized up to USD 250 million of debt repurchases through 2027, and the company repurchased USD 120 million of notes at par in July 2026. The pro forma figure after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment is USD 5,675 million, or 8.48x; the figure after the 2026-07-21 repurchase is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11

facts.text: Revenue durability depends on fee contracts and the election cycle. Retransmission consent and network affiliation economics set the cash margin, and political advertising swings earnings between even and odd years, so the 2027 off-year and the renewals of network agreements from mid-2027 to the end of 2028 are the periods in which refinancing and earnings pressures meet. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is that 2026 is an election year with political advertising already at USD 113 million in the first half against USD 22 million, and the company guides third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million and the guided revenue implies growth of 24.83% to 28.84% over the prior-year quarter. If those results are met and the revolver balance proves small, last-twelve-months earnings would rise sharply and leverage would fall, and the issuer's covenant total net leverage of 5.73x already sits below its 7.00x incurrence level. The view would improve if reported results meet guidance and debt is reduced from cash flow, and worsen if third quarter revenue misses the low end of guidance, if the revolver is drawn further, or if affiliation renewals raise network fees faster than retransmission revenue. Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 37; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

# GRAY MEDIA, INC (gtn) - Source readiness as of 2026-11-05
## Request

GRAY MEDIA, INC (issuer id gtn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the seven supplied filings and earnings releases support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work, and what stays out of reach.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work for GRAY MEDIA, INC, but only to the second quarter of 2026 and without executed debt documents, ratings or market data.

The latest balance sheet is dated 128 days before the as-of date, and a July 2026 revolver borrowing is not quantified, so liquidity and leverage conclusions carry that caveat. Covenant capacity, ratings, market-implied risk and committee sizing cannot be supported from these sources.
Basis: calculation C1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25
### Key findings

The financial record supports a four-quarter view. The third and fourth quarters of 2025 and the first and second quarters of 2026 each have a filed report or release, and the quarterly revenue figures tie to the annual and year-to-date totals with no difference.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4

The instrument record is complete for the second quarter of 2026. The debt note lists every term loan and note series, with total principal of USD 5,867 million and maturities by year, and the credit agreement leverage table is printed, so Financial foundation can use the filed figures instead of rebuilding them.

Two net debt figures are printed for the same date. The credit agreement table gives USD 5,696 million after letters of credit of USD 5 million and cash of USD 176 million, while the earnings release gives USD 5,691 million before letters of credit, so each analytical module must name the definition it uses.
Basis: calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 4

After the quarter end the company repurchased USD 120 million of notes on 2026-07-21, using cash on hand and borrowings under the revolving credit facility. The borrowed amount is not stated, so the USD 745 million of availability reported at 2026-06-30 cannot be carried forward as current liquidity.
Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 33–34

The proxy statement that carries board, compensation and ownership detail is incorporated by reference in the annual report and was not supplied, so Business & governance rests on the annual report's business, risk factor and legal proceedings sections.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 116
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

Nothing in the supplied documents contradicts the readiness view. It would change if a quarterly report for the period ended 2026-09-30 or a later filing dated on or before 2026-11-05 exists and shows a different revolver balance or new financing, or if the executed credit agreement and indentures define covenant terms differently from the filing summaries.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 35
### Limitations
- The supplied set ends with the filings of 2026-08-07, which is 90 days before the as-of date, so events after that date are not established.
- The credit agreement and indentures were not supplied; covenant tests, guarantees and security are known only as the filings summarise them.
- No credit ratings, market prices, peer set or portfolio limits were supplied, so work that depends on them is not supported.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt of USD 5,632 million at 2026-06-30 is 8.42x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, against 4.90x at FY2024, because the 2024 political-year earnings rolled off while debt rose. The issuer's covenant measure of 5.73x is lower because it divides by a pro forma eight-quarter average of USD 994 million.

Reported EBITDA covers cash interest paid only 1.74x over the last twelve months. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was cash of USD 176 million and revolver availability of USD 745 million, before a July 2026 repurchase that the company partly funded from the revolver in an amount it does not state.

### Credit read-through

Leverage on the basis a creditor carries has deteriorated sharply. Net debt moved from USD 5,486 million at FY2024 to USD 5,376 million at FY2025 and USD 5,632 million at 2026-06-30, while reported EBITDA fell from USD 1,120 million to USD 629 million as political advertising dropped from USD 497 million to USD 42 million, so net debt over reported EBITDA rose from 4.90x to 8.55x and stood at 8.42x on the last twelve months. The cyclical earnings swing, not new borrowing, drives most of the change, which means the ratio should improve only if the 2026 election-year advertising lifts the twelve-month figure.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C24; calculation C25; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 73

Coverage is the thinner dimension. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.84x at FY2024, 1.60x at FY2025 and 1.74x over the last twelve months, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA covered it 1.84x on the same twelve months, so a further earnings shortfall would leave little margin before cash flow after interest turns negative. Operating cash flow over the last twelve months was USD 250 million against purchases of property and equipment of USD 104 million, which leaves little to fund the common and preferred dividends.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 94

Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was cash of USD 176 million plus USD 745 million of revolver availability, with the USD 400 million securitization facility fully drawn, so the facilities already carry funding that sits outside reported debt. The 2026-07-21 repurchase of USD 120 million of notes was funded in part from the revolver in an amount the filings do not state, so current availability is lower than the reported figure by an amount that is not established. Maturities are light until 2028, when USD 739 million of term loan and the revolver fall due, which concentrates refinancing risk in the next political cycle.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C18; calculation C28

The issuer's own leverage measures tell a milder story than the reported figures. Its covenant total net leverage of 5.73x and first lien net leverage of 2.55x rest on a denominator that averages eight quarters and adds pro forma acquisition earnings and expected synergies, so they measure compliance headroom on a smoothed, pro forma earnings base rather than leverage on current reported earnings. Covenant capacity is not inferred from them because the credit agreement was not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C19

Acquisitions add debt capacity pressure before they add earnings. The company spent USD 264 million of cash on acquisitions in the 2026 six months, issued USD 70 million of additional 2033 first lien notes on 2026-06-30 and paid USD 43 million in cash on 2026-07-01 for further stations, so pro forma net debt of USD 5,675 million, or 8.48x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, already exceeds the reported 2026-06-30 figure before any acquired earnings are included.
Basis: calculation C20; calculation C22; calculation C27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 15; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

Contrary evidence is that revenue grew 3.41% in the 2026 six months and issuer-adjusted EBITDA grew from USD 329 million to USD 368 million, with political advertising at USD 113 million against USD 22 million a year earlier, so the twelve-month denominator should keep rising through the second half of 2026. What would make the view wrong is a second-half political result well above the guided range, or debt reduction from the USD 250 million repurchase authorization; what would confirm it is further revolver borrowing to fund repurchases or acquisitions.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C23; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5

## Findings
### Bottom line

Gray Media is a sturdy station operator whose scale and market positions support creditors, but family-influenced control, a ten-vote share class and debt-funded station purchases beside maintained dividends make sponsor and governance risk medium.

Creditors rely on management policy rather than documented limits, because the debt agreements and the proxy statement were not supplied. The risk would rise if acquisitions keep being funded with secured debt while dividends continue, and would fall with documented debt reduction.
### Key findings

The operating business is the credit's strength: the stations are well diversified, with the largest market at 5% of revenue and the ten largest markets at about 25%, and most markets are led by a first or second ranked station. That breadth lowers the chance that one local market or one advertiser damages debt service.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 4

Half of revenue is now fee income negotiated with distributors and networks rather than advertising, which makes renewals the main business risk. Retransmission consent revenue was 46.17% of FY2025 revenue and network affiliation fees took 28.50% of it, so net retransmission revenue of USD 547 million depends on subscriber trends and on affiliation agreements that expire from mid-2027 to the end of 2028, the same window in which the 2028 term loan and revolver mature.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2

Earnings swing with the election cycle, so a single year says little about debt service. Political advertising was USD 497 million, or 13.64% of revenue, in FY2024 and USD 42 million, or 1.36%, in FY2025, so creditors should read leverage across the full two-year cycle and not on an election year alone.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2

Voting control sits with the Class A holders and the Howell-Robinson Family, whose stake is not established. Each Class A share carries ten votes, which gives that class 51.45% of votes on the share counts at 2026-07-31, and the filing states that the Howell-Robinson Family can exert significant influence over policies and management. Creditors therefore face shareholder decisions on acquisitions, dividends and leverage that are not checked by an outside controlling holder, and a change of control would trigger mandatory redemption of the USD 600 million Series A preferred stock.
Basis: calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38, 98; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2

Financial policy is mixed: growth is funded partly with secured debt while shareholders are paid. The company bought stations for USD 280 million of stated consideration in the first half of 2026, issued USD 70 million of first lien notes to fund the American Spirit Media closing and a preferred stock repurchase, and paid common dividends of USD 33 million and preferred dividends of USD 52 million in FY2025. The preferred repurchase paid USD 30 million for USD 50 million of liquidation preference, which cut junior claims and the cash dividend by USD 4 million a year, but the new first lien debt ranks ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 15, 18

Reporting quality supports monitoring. The auditor has served since 2006, disclosure controls were found effective at year end, and the quarterly report and earnings release print the covenant leverage calculation in full, so creditors can follow covenant ratios each quarter even though the debt documents were not supplied.

Licence dependence and regulation tie the asset value to the FCC. Broadcast licences and goodwill were 78.15% of total assets at 2026-06-30, the national ownership limit of 39% of households (with a discount for UHF stations) caps further scale, and the second closings of the latest acquisitions await regulatory approval, so deal-funded growth depends on rule changes that management expects but the filings do not guarantee.
Basis: calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower risk reading is the operating record and the preference for reducing junior claims: the preferred repurchase was done at a 40.00% discount to liquidation preference, the board authorized up to USD 250 million of debt repurchases through 2027, and the company repurchased USD 120 million of notes at par in July 2026. The view would move to low risk if debt reduction continued from operating cash flow without secured debt issuance, and to high risk if debt-funded acquisitions or a distribution were funded ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes, or if the proxy statement showed the family holding a controlling majority of votes.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 25; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Limitations

- The family's percentage holding, board independence, committee structure and pay arrangements are not established because the proxy statement was not supplied, so the control assessment rests on voting rights and risk factor wording and could be understated or overstated.

- Funding for most of the 2026 station purchases is described only as cash or new notes, and acquired earnings are not disclosed, so the leverage effect of the acquisition programme on creditors cannot be sized here.
- The holder of the Series A preferred stock is not named in the supplied documents, so whether the preferred holder aligns with creditors in a stress or in a sale is not established.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In the first half of 2026 the company closed station purchases with stated consideration of USD 280 million: WBBJ USD 27 million, three Allen Media stations USD 56 million, seven Allen Media markets USD 115 million, Block Communications stations USD 80 million and Sagamore Hill stations USD 2 million. It also swapped three stations to Scripps for two others without cash, recording a non-cash loss of USD 22 million.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13

On 2026-06-30 the company issued USD 70 million of additional 7.25% first lien notes due 2033 at par in a private placement. The proceeds paid USD 40 million of the first closing of the American Spirit Media acquisition and USD 30 million to repurchase 50,000 Series A preferred shares with USD 50 million of liquidation preference. On 2026-07-01 the first closing of American Spirit Media and WHPM was paid in cash, and USD 11 million remains payable at the second closings, which need regulatory approval.
Basis: calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18, 25; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

In 2025 the company refinanced most debt: USD 900 million and USD 250 million of 9.625% second lien notes due 2032, USD 775 million of 7.25% first lien notes due 2033, and a revolving credit facility raised to USD 750 million and extended to 2028-12-01. The proceeds redeemed the 2027 notes at par, repaid term loans and redeemed part of the 2029 first lien notes at 103% of par. Later in 2026 the company repurchased USD 100 million of 2029 first lien notes and USD 20 million of 2031 notes at par.

## Request

GRAY MEDIA, INC (issuer id gtn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit view built on the earlier source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work, with the supporting filings.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Gray Media's credit is adequate on business quality but weak on balance sheet strain, with net debt at 8.42x reported EBITDA and cover of 1.74x, so creditors depend on election-year earnings and timely refinancing of the 2028 maturities.

Net debt was USD 5,632 million at 2026-06-30 and, pro forma for the cash paid for acquisitions on 2026-07-01, USD 5,675 million, or 8.48x; the effect of the revolver-funded repurchase of 2026-07-21 on net debt and on cash is not established. The offsets are top-ranked stations in diversified markets, no principal due before 2028 and, at 2026-06-30, revolver availability of USD 745 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4
### Key findings

Leverage is high on both reported and adjusted earnings. Net debt over reported EBITDA was 4.90x at FY2024, 8.55x at FY2025 and 8.42x on the last twelve months, and 7.94x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, because reported EBITDA fell 43.84% as political advertising fell 91.55%, so creditors carry the debt on off-year earnings until 2026 political revenue is booked. The pro forma figure after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment is USD 5,675 million, or 8.48x; the figure after the 2026-07-21 repurchase is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11

Interest cover is the thinnest dimension. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.84x at FY2024, 1.60x at FY2025 and 1.74x on the last twelve months, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 1.84x, so a repeat of the off-year trough would leave little room for a cost or revenue miss. Cash interest takes 12.23% of last-twelve-months revenue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12

Free cash flow is positive but small relative to the debt. Operating cash flow of USD 250 million less capital spending of USD 104 million gave USD 146 million over the last twelve months, and after USD 87 million of common and preferred dividends only USD 59 million remained, so deleveraging from internal cash flow is slow unless earnings rise. The FY2025 off-year left USD 96 million after the same items.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C9

The maturity profile is the main support. No principal falls due before 2028, the USD 739 million term loan and the USD 750 million revolver are both due on 2028-12-01, and the USD 1,125 million of 2029 first lien notes follow, so USD 1,864 million, or 31.77% of principal, comes due by the end of 2029. Secured debt is 65.78% of principal, so the unsecured notes of USD 2,008 million rank behind a large secured layer.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 37

Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was USD 921 million, made of cash and revolver availability, before the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment and the July 2026 repurchase funded partly from the revolver, so cash after those events is not established. The receivables securitization of USD 400 million is fully drawn, so it adds no further funding, and the revolver amount drawn is not stated, so liquidity today is not established.
Basis: calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 25, 33–34; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

Revenue durability depends on fee contracts and the election cycle. Retransmission consent and network affiliation economics set the cash margin, and political advertising swings earnings between even and odd years, so the 2027 off-year and the renewals of network agreements from mid-2027 to the end of 2028 are the periods in which refinancing and earnings pressures meet. Management guidance for the third quarter of 2026 points to revenue of USD 935 million to USD 965 million against USD 749 million a year earlier, which is guidance and not an outcome.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5

Governance and financial policy are mixed and add to the balance sheet risk. The earlier assessment rates sponsor and governance risk as medium because acquisitions were funded partly with first lien notes while dividends continued, and because a ten-vote share class concentrates voting power; the preferred stock repurchase at a discount and the debt repurchases are the countervailing actions.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is that 2026 is an election year with political advertising already at USD 113 million in the first half against USD 22 million, and the company guides third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million and the guided revenue implies growth of 24.83% to 28.84% over the prior-year quarter. If those results are met and the revolver balance proves small, last-twelve-months earnings would rise sharply and leverage would fall, and the issuer's covenant total net leverage of 5.73x already sits below its 7.00x incurrence level. The view would improve if reported results meet guidance and debt is reduced from cash flow, and worsen if third quarter revenue misses the low end of guidance, if the revolver is drawn further, or if affiliation renewals raise network fees faster than retransmission revenue.
Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 37; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6
### Limitations

- The financial profile rests on twelve-month figures that include a quarter in which acquired stations contributed only part of a period, so the leverage and cover ratios may overstate or understate the run rate of the enlarged group.

- Ratings, market prices and peer benchmarks were not part of the evidence, so the view is an absolute fundamental assessment and says nothing about how the debt trades or compares with similar broadcasters.

- The tests that govern distributions, additional debt and liens are known only from filing summaries, so the downside path assumes management policy rather than testing what the documents would allow.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Scale and market rank are a strength. The group reaches about 37% of US households and holds the top-rated station in 77 markets, with no market above 5% of revenue, so a local downturn or one lost advertiser does little to debt service and the stations keep bargaining power with distributors, which supports refinancing access.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 4

A back-ended maturity profile is a strength. No principal is due before 2028 and USD 1,864 million falls due by the end of 2029, so the company does not need the capital markets in the 2026 cycle, which lowers near-term default risk even though leverage is high.
Basis: calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 16

A path to higher earnings in the current cycle is a strength. Political advertising of USD 113 million in the first half of 2026 and guided third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million would lift twelve-month earnings and cover if realised, which gives management a credible route to deleveraging without asset sales.

Leverage and cover on reported earnings are the main weakness. Net debt of 8.42x reported EBITDA (8.48x pro forma after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment) and cover of 1.74x leave little tolerance for a miss, so a fall in earnings would raise leverage and squeeze free cash flow before any covenant is tested.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

Dependence on fee contracts and the cycle is a weakness. Retransmission consent revenue was 46.17% of FY2025 revenue and network fees took a large share of it, with political advertising 1.36% of revenue in the off-year, so earnings can fall by 43.84% between an election year and the following year and renewals can reset fees.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C16

Policy and secured-debt priority are a weakness. Acquisitions funded partly with first lien notes and maintained dividends raise secured debt ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes, and the family-influenced control structure means these choices are decided by shareholders, so recovery for junior creditors is more exposed.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

### Business and operating model read

The revenue base is a large station group with two fee lines and one cyclical line. Core advertising of USD 1,452 million and retransmission consent revenue of USD 1,429 million supply 46.91% and 46.17% of FY2025 revenue, political advertising swings by even and odd years, and network affiliation fees of USD 882 million are the largest cost, so net retransmission revenue of USD 547 million is the margin that matters. Pricing power sits partly with the group, which negotiates retransmission with distributors, and partly with the networks that set affiliation fees at renewal.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C17; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2

Cost flexibility is limited because network fees and station staffing are largely fixed in the short run, so earnings move more than revenue: reported EBITDA fell 43.84% when revenue fell 15.07% between FY2024 and FY2025. Capital intensity is modest, with USD 108 million of purchases of property and equipment in FY2025, which leaves operating cash flow available for interest, dividends and acquisitions, but conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow is low after USD 385 million of cash interest.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 75
### Industry forces

Supplier power is high: the four major networks set affiliation fees and the agreements expire between mid-2027 and the end of 2028, so renewals can move USD 882 million of annual cost. Buyer power rests with distributors: retransmission revenue fell in the first half of 2026 on subscriber declines, a station moving to independent status and a resolved dispute, so the largest fee line is under pressure. Entry barriers are real because broadcast licences are limited in each area and ownership rules cap national reach, but the same rules limit the group's ability to buy more stations.

Policy and the economy matter through two channels. Advertising budgets follow the economy, and the election cycle supplies political revenue in even years, so regulation of ownership and the timing of pending station approvals affect growth plans that management has linked to expected ownership reform. These factors support a view that growth depends on regulators and the cycle rather than on organic share gains.
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwind is the 2026 election cycle, with first-half political advertising of USD 113 million and guided third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million, and the headwinds are the 2027 off-year, subscriber declines and the maturity of the term loan and revolver on 2028-12-01. Over three to five years the outcome depends on whether network and distributor renewals leave net retransmission revenue intact and whether acquisitions add earnings that exceed their secured-debt cost, which is not disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with the 2027 off-year: political advertising reverts to the FY2025 level of USD 42 million, and retransmission revenue falls further as subscriber declines continue while network renewals begin. Revenue and reported EBITDA would then move toward the FY2025 outcome, when reported EBITDA of USD 629 million covered cash interest only 1.60x. Free cash flow after dividends was USD 96 million in that off-year, so the group avoids liquidity distress if it holds acquisitions and repurchases to cash flow, but a revolver-funded repurchase or purchase would reduce the USD 745 million of availability just as the term loan and revolver approach their 2028-12-01 maturity. Management levers are suspending the common dividend of USD 33 million, using the USD 250 million repurchase authorization more sparingly and delaying acquisitions; these are possible but not documented.
Basis: calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 75; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Overall credit view

Overall, GRAY MEDIA, INC presents an adequate business profile supported by top-ranked stations, diversified markets and a back-ended maturity profile, but credit quality is constrained by net debt of 8.42x reported EBITDA (8.48x pro forma after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment), cover of 1.74x and secured debt of 65.78% of principal. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in election years and weak in off-years because political revenue and fee renewals drive earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2026 election-year result, the revolver balance and renewals of network and distributor contracts. The primary downside path is an off-year earnings trough in 2027 that coincides with a drawn revolver ahead of the 2028-12-01 maturity. Further analysis would require the revolver balance after 2026-07-21, third quarter 2026 results, the executed debt documents and the proxy statement. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 maturities from a weak off-year earnings base with a drawn revolver.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C8
